title: 🤖 macOS: Fix crash when running `--embedded` without a debugger connection
body:
> [!INFO] *AI disclosure*: This contribution was authored by an autonomous AI agent, on behalf of a user, to fix a crash they hit while using `--embedded` to render a Godot project without an on-screen window.

### Bug

On macOS, starting the engine with `--embedded` outside the editor crashes immediately, while the display server is still being created:

```
handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 11
```

The backtrace symbolizes into MoltenVK frames, which makes it look like a rendering or shader-compilation fault. It is not — it is a null dereference.

`DisplayServerMacOSEmbedded` reports back to the editor over the debugger connection (`game_view:set_context_id`, cursor, mouse mode, IME). Those call sites dereference `EngineDebugger::get_singleton()` unconditionally, but the singleton only exists when the process was started by the editor. The first one runs in the constructor, so the crash happens before anything is drawn.

`OS_MacOS_Embedded::alert()` already guards its own message with exactly this check, so the "no debugger" case was anticipated on the OS side but missed in the display server.

### Fix

Route the seven messages through a small helper that drops them when there is no debugger, matching the existing style in `os_macos.mm`. Editor-hosted embedding is unaffected — the singleton is present there and every message is sent as before.

### Result

`--embedded` now runs standalone and renders normally into its off-screen layer, with no window of its own. That makes it usable for scripted runs and screenshot capture on a machine where an extra window would steal focus — close to what [godot-proposals#5790](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/5790) asks for, using machinery the engine already has.

### Testing

Tested on macOS 26.6.2, Apple M4 Pro, built from `4.7.2-stable` with the same patch.

Before: crash on startup, as above.
After: the project runs to completion and a screenshot saved from the root viewport shows the scene rendered correctly (Metal, Forward+, ~113 fps).

```
godot --embedded --path <project> --script <capture.gd> --resolution 1280x720
```

Where `capture.gd` is a `SceneTree` script that instantiates a scene, waits some frames, and calls `root.get_texture().get_image().save_png(...)`.

No automated test is included: the engine's test suite drives display servers through `DisplayServerMock` on top of `DisplayServerHeadless`, and exercising `DisplayServerMacOSEmbedded` needs a real CoreAnimation/Metal context on macOS, which the headless test runner does not provide. Happy to add one if there is a harness for this that I have missed.

### Notes for reviewers

- The commit is against `master`; it was compiled and run against `4.7.2-stable`, where the code is identical apart from context lines.
